beats: Aggressive pass rushers, especially on 3rd & short near the goal line, when the defense expects a pass. For the drill, log it as a Pass (that's how the stats count it), and it's a great bonus call when the defense is selling out to rush.
caption: White arrows: the linemen block forward and the slot receiver runs across behind the line. Dashed white: the underhand toss. Yellow dashes: pass rushers charging the QB.
name: Shovel pass
seenIn: Covered together while going over Eagles at Bears, Week 3 (Luther Burden’s 8-yard touchdown on 3rd & 2)
spot: A receiver or back running sideways behind the line right as the QB moves forward (not back) with the ball. On the replay, look for the QB flipping the ball underhand.

what: A shovel pass is a tiny forward pass, tossed underhand, to a player running across just behind the line of scrimmage. It's officially a pass, but it looks and works like a run.
The linemen block forward as if it's a run. The pass rushers, sure it's a pass, charge the quarterback, and the ball goes right underneath them to a player heading for the hole they just left.
